purpose: Compare two verified property states across different dates or defined states and identify material changes, evidence and legal events without projecting current facts backward.
core_principle: STATE A → DIFFERENCE → CAUSING EVENT(S) → LEGAL EFFECT → STATE B
rules: Both comparison states must refer to the same verified property scope.
State dates remain explicit; current state must not be projected backward.
A difference is not automatically attributed to an event until evidence supports the link.
Legal effect must be checked against the law applicable to the relevant event/date.
Registration changes must be distinguished from underlying transactions or succession events.
A comparison may show that a change occurred without establishing why if the causal evidence is incomplete.
Different property interests may change independently between the two states.
Historical state comparison requires historical evidence appropriate to both endpoints.
hard_stops: Never compare two properties merely because addresses match.
Never infer a causal event solely from the difference between two records.
Never use today's state as historical State A without evidence.
Never treat a transfer document as proof of the registered State B without registration evidence where required.
